writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 162 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
As requirements for job applications are getting increasingly higher, college students ought to be better prepared for their future career. In an era when employers demand not only a diploma but also practical competence, waiting until graduation to think about work is simply too late.
There are concrete steps every student can take. To begin with, obtaining relevant certificates and mastering professional skills builds a solid foundation. Last summer, for instance, I taught myself data analysis and earned a certificate, which later helped me stand out in an internship interview. What is more, internships offer irreplaceable experience: by working in a real company, students learn how a workplace actually operates and discover which career truly suits them. Such preparation turns abstract knowledge into employable ability.
In conclusion, the fiercer competition becomes, the more valuable early preparation is. Therefore, college students should seize every chance to enrich their skills and experience, so that when opportunity knocks, they are ready to open the door.

transcripts.head: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

lines.en: M: Good morning. My name is Bob Fetterman. I'm the computer technician.
lines.zh: M：早上好。我叫鲍勃·费特曼，是电脑技术员。

lines.en: W: Didn't I call for you last week?
lines.zh: W：上周不是我打电话叫你来的吗？

lines.en: M: Maybe? I work for Alpha Maintenance. I imagine someone from your office called our central office and I'm the engineer designated to your case.
lines.zh: M：可能吧？我为 Alpha Maintenance 工作。我想应该是你们办公室有人打电话给了我们的总部，而我是负责处理你们这个问题的工程师。

lines.en: W: Yeah, I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday, which is now 10 days ago. I made it clear it was an urgent matter and please send someone as soon as possible. Couldn't you or someone else have come sooner?
lines.zh: W：是的，我上周二，也就是十天前，跟那边的一位女士谈过。我明确说过这是件急事，请尽快派人过来。你或者其他人就不能早点来吗？

lines.en: M: I'm sorry, but I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics. I simply do not know. All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could.
lines.zh: M：很抱歉，但我不负责安排所有的后勤事宜。我确实不知道。我只能告诉你，我是这周接到电话的，并且已经尽可能快地赶来了。

lines.en: W: I see. Well, I'll have you know, my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come. I understand it might not be your fault, but nevertheless, you should know what the feeling is around here.
lines.zh: W：我明白了。不过我要告诉你，我的经理对你们花了这么长时间才过来相当不满。我知道这可能不是你的错，但不管怎样，你应该知道这里对此事的看法。

lines.en: M: I understand, and I'm sorry for any inconvenience. I will try to resolve your computer problem as swiftly and optimally as I can. What and where is the issue?
lines.zh: M：我明白，也很抱歉给你带来不便。我会尽我所能，尽快、妥善地解决你们的电脑问题。问题是什么，在哪里？

lines.en: W: It's this machine right here. It was running slow for a while, I guess, and gradually got worse and worse. Last Tuesday, it just stopped working altogether. If you switch it on, you will see what I mean.
lines.zh: W：就是这台机器。它运行缓慢有一阵子了，我想，然后逐渐变得越来越糟。上周二，它彻底停止工作了。你把它打开就知道我说的是什么意思了。

lines.en: M: Okay. Do you know if it's backed up?
lines.zh: M：好的。你知道它有没有备份吗？

lines.en: W: Backed up?
lines.zh: W：备份？

lines.en: M: I mean, do you know if its contents have been copied and saved somewhere else?
lines.zh: M：我的意思是，你知道里面的内容有没有被复制并保存到其他地方吗？

lines.en: W: I don't know.
lines.zh: W：我不知道。

lines.en: M: Well, depending on the ensuing operative scenario, if I need to wipe the system directories clean in order to reconfigure default protocols, then my first intervention should be to intricately retrieve all inventories that I can. Otherwise, all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost.
lines.zh: M：这个嘛，具体要看接下来采取什么操作。如果我需要清空系统目录，以便重新配置默认协议，那么我的第一步应该是尽可能仔细地找回所有资料。否则，存储在硬盘上的所有数据都会永久丢失。

lines.en: W: My manager would know. Let me go get him.
lines.zh: W：我的经理应该知道。我去把他叫来。

transcripts.head: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

lines.en: M: Have you given more thought to studying law?
lines.zh: M: 你有没有进一步考虑过学法律？

lines.en: W: I've been thinking about it a lot, yes. In fact, this is why I wished to speak to you. I wanted to hear more about what it's like.
lines.zh: W: 我确实认真考虑过很多次。事实上，这就是我想和你谈谈的原因。我想多了解一下这个职业到底是什么样的。

lines.en: M: A career in law is a beautiful thing in my opinion. Many people will say it's a boring field, but I disagree. The thing is there are many different branches of law and many different jobs.
lines.zh: M: 在我看来，从事法律工作是一件很美好的事。很多人会说这是个无聊的领域，但我不这么认为。问题在于，法律有许多不同的分支，也有许多不同的工作。

lines.en: W: You are involved with buildings and construction, right?
lines.zh: W: 你是从事建筑和施工方面工作的，对吧？

lines.en: M: Correct. I'm a solicitor, specializing in real estate. Most of my work involves mediating land disputes.
lines.zh: M: 没错。我是一名事务律师，专门从事房地产法律事务。我的大部分工作都涉及调解土地纠纷。

lines.en: W: Do you mind giving me an example?
lines.zh: W: 你介意举个例子吗？

lines.en: M: Sure. So in many cases I am employed to arbitrate between two clashing parties. Let's say for example, there are two landowners who are in a thorny disagreement about something like the borders of their adjacent plots. Someone may employ me to break the deadlock and resolve the dispute. Often my work involves negotiating agreements, plain and simple.
lines.zh: M: 当然可以。很多时候，我会受雇在两个发生冲突的当事人之间进行仲裁。比如说，有两位土地所有者，因为相邻地块的边界之类的问题而陷入棘手的争执。有人可能会聘请我来打破僵局，解决这场纠纷。很多时候，我的工作就是协商达成协议，仅此而已。

lines.en: W: So you are saying that a lot of what you do is fix people's legal issues, like you try to find a solution that benefits everyone and that prevents a problem from escalating.
lines.zh: W: 所以你的意思是，你所做的很多事情都是在解决人们的法律问题，比如努力找到一个对大家都有利的解决方案，防止问题进一步恶化。

lines.en: M: Exactly, well put. You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive. For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible.
lines.zh: M: 没错，你说得很准确。你要记住，法院和所有官僚机构一样，往往会非常混乱、令人沮丧，而且费用高昂。因此，只要有可能，通常最好在法院之外解决问题。

lines.en: W: I see. So besides knowing the law inside out, you need good people skills, right?
lines.zh: W: 我明白了。所以除了要对法律了如指掌之外，还需要有很好的人际交往能力，对吧？

lines.en: M: Of course. Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument.
lines.zh: M: 当然。任何涉及与人打交道的工作都需要良好的人际交往能力，而任何法律从业者都需要非常善于清晰、有说服力地表达自己的观点。

lines.en: W: Right. So I've been thinking about studying criminal law. I think it sounds very interesting.
lines.zh: W: 对。所以我一直在考虑学习刑法。我觉得这听起来很有意思。

lines.en: M: Mm-hmm, yes. I'd say there's more money in property law, but the stakes are higher in criminal law. I can see how you would find it more interesting.
lines.zh: M: 嗯，是的。我想房地产法能赚更多钱，但刑法涉及的利害关系更大。我能理解你为什么会觉得它更有趣。

transcripts.head: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

lines.en: When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant information. But as we age, many of us have difficulty retrieving memories.
lines.zh: 当一个人试图提取一段记忆时，其大脑会迅速检查其中储存的所有内容，以找出相关信息。但随着年龄增长，我们中的许多人会难以回忆起记忆。

lines.en: In a review published in the journal *Trends in Cognitive Sciences* on February 11th, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories. While this wealth of prior knowledge can make memory retrieval challenging, the researchers say it has its upsides—this life experience can aid with creativity and decision-making.
lines.zh: 研究人员在2月11日发表于《认知科学趋势》杂志的一篇综述中提出了这一现象可能发生的原因：老年人的大脑会为积累的知识分配更多空间，因此在尝试提取记忆时需要在更多内容中进行搜索。研究人员表示，尽管这些丰富的既有知识会使记忆提取变得更具挑战性，但它也有积极的一面——这些人生经历能够帮助人们进行创造和决策。

lines.en: Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain imaging studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it. The studies also showed that when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge than younger adults do.
lines.zh: 研究人员塔雷克·阿梅尔、乔丹娜·温和林恩·哈舍尔考察了多项行为研究和脑成像研究。这些研究显示，老年人难以抑制已经不再相关的信息；在寻找某一特定记忆时，他们常常会连同其他无关记忆一起提取出来。研究还显示，在面对认知任务时，老年人比年轻人更加依赖既有知识。

lines.en: While the researchers focus primarily on the difficulties that these disorderly, crowded memories may pose, they also highlight a few situations in which these same memory patterns may be useful. "Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories," the researchers write. They further hypothesize that older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to decision-making, where they can pull on their accumulated wisdom.
lines.zh: 尽管研究人员主要关注这些杂乱、拥挤的记忆可能造成的困难，但他们也指出了几种相同记忆模式可能发挥作用的情形。研究人员写道：“证据表明，老年人的创造力得益于记忆内容的丰富，不仅得以保持，有时还会有所增强。”他们进一步推测，在进行决策时，老年人可能会受益于自己的既有知识，因为他们能够运用积累的智慧。

transcripts.head: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

lines.en: There are at least four major problems with work in America today.
lines.zh: 如今，美国的工作至少存在四个主要问题。

lines.en: First, work can be alienating. Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work.
lines.zh: 首先，工作可能导致异化。劳动者往往无法掌控自己的工作方式、工作时间、对其生产的商品和服务的处置方式，以及对其劳动所创造利润的处置方式。

lines.en: Second, workers are not paid the full value of their labor. Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality and a decline in labor's share of income.
lines.zh: 其次，劳动者没有获得其劳动的全部价值。实际工资未能与生产率同步增长，导致经济不平等加剧，并使劳动收入在总收入中的占比下降。

lines.en: Third, people are time poor. In the U.S., full time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day despite productivity increases. Long working hours contribute to the feeling of "time poverty", which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being.
lines.zh: 第三，人们缺乏时间。尽管生产率有所提高，美国的全职雇员每天平均工作8.72小时。长时间工作加剧了“时间贫困”感，并对心理健康产生不利影响。

lines.en: Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk. Technological innovation could in theory liberate people from the 40-hour work week. But unless changes are made to the structure of work, automation will simply exert downward pressure on wages and further diminish work opportunities.
lines.zh: 第四，自动化使工作岗位和工资面临风险。从理论上说，技术创新可以使人们摆脱每周40小时的工作制。但是，除非对工作结构进行改变，否则自动化只会给工资施加下行压力，并进一步减少工作机会。

lines.en: So, what can be done to alleviate these problems? There are competing visions of the best way to arrive at a solution. One vision is what's known as the "post-work" position. The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time. They assert that although doing some work might be necessary, meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace. Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.
lines.zh: 那么，可以采取什么措施来缓解这些问题呢？对于如何实现解决方案，人们存在相互竞争的构想。其中一种构想被称为“后工作”立场。后工作理论家认为，工作不应在我们的生活中占据核心地位，也不应占用我们如此多的时间。他们主张，尽管从事一定的工作可能是必要的，但意义、目标和社会价值存在于工作场所以外建立并维系的社区和关系之中。因此，生活本身应被视为目的。

lines.en: Recent studies show that self-control and persistence increase academic outcomes, independence of IQ. Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes. Children who think effort leads to achievement outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait. Given the link between persistence and academic success, decisions about efforts are particularly important in childhood.
lines.zh: 近期研究表明，自我控制和坚持不懈能够提升学业表现，而这一作用独立于智商。甚至我们对努力的个人看法也会影响学业表现。认为努力能够带来成就的儿童，比那些认为能力是一种固定特质的儿童表现更好。鉴于坚持不懈与学业成功之间的联系，童年时期对是否付出努力的判断尤为重要。

lines.en: Yet, relatively little research has explored how young children learn what's worth the effort. We all know that infants are keen observers of the social world, but they're not just idly watching; they are tiny learning machines. They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples. Even a 15-month-old infant can outperform a high level computer in such tasks. Could infants also make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort? If so, then maybe persistence isn't simply a character trait. Maybe it's flexible and adaptable based on social context.
lines.zh: 然而，相对而言，很少有研究探讨幼儿是如何学会判断什么值得付出努力的。我们都知道，婴儿善于观察社会世界，但他们并非只是无所事事地观看；他们是微型的学习机器。他们仅凭几个例子，就能概括出因果关系和社会角色等抽象概念。即使是15个月大的婴儿，在这类任务中的表现也可能超过高水平的计算机。当涉及努力时，婴儿是否也能根据少数几个例子作出广泛且可推广的推断？如果可以，那么坚持不懈也许并不只是某种性格特征，而是会根据社会情境灵活调整、适应变化的能力。

lines.en: To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things—an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal. Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top. The button could be pressed down, but didn't actually activate anything. Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music. We gave the babies the music toy and left the room. Then analysts who didn't know which condition each baby was in, watched video tapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button.
lines.zh: 为了探究这一问题，我们向15个月大的婴儿展示两种情形中的一种：一名实验者努力工作以实现两个不同的目标，或者一名毫不费力地实现每个目标的实验者。随后，我们向婴儿介绍一个新颖的音乐玩具，看起来似乎可以通过按下顶部的大按钮来启动。这个按钮可以被按下，但实际上并不会启动任何功能。在婴儿看不见的地方，我们用一个隐藏按钮打开了音乐玩具，让他们听到玩具发出音乐。我们把音乐玩具交给婴儿，然后离开房间。之后，不知道每个婴儿属于哪种实验条件的分析人员观看了实验录像，并统计婴儿试图通过按下按钮启动玩具的次数。

lines.en: Across one study and a pre-registered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed push the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed. In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding. Part of what's exciting about this finding is that the babies didn't just imitate the adult's actions. Instead, they generalized the value of effort to a novel task. The experimenter never demonstrated pushing a button or trying to make music. Instead, the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions that the new toy probably also required persistence.
lines.zh: 在一项研究及其预注册重复实验中，看过成年人坚持不懈并取得成功的婴儿，按下按钮的次数约为看过成年人毫不费力地取得成功的婴儿的两倍。换言之，婴儿仅仅观察成年人努力工作并取得成功的两个例子后，就学会了努力是有价值的。这一发现令人兴奋的部分原因在于，婴儿并不只是模仿成年人的动作。相反，他们把努力的价值推广到了一个全新的任务中。实验者从未示范按按钮或尝试让玩具播放音乐。相反，婴儿从不同的努力行为示例中学到，这个新玩具可能也需要坚持不懈。

lines.en: If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more. If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes.
lines.zh: 如果长期迟到已经占据了你的生活，并变成了定义你这个人的特征，那么你很可能正因此错失工作机会、休闲活动、友谊以及更多其他东西。如果你在自己的人生中都迟到，请做好组织安排，优先重视守时，并处理任何潜在原因。

lines.en: When you have to be somewhere, try to arrive 15 to 30 minutes before you need to. If you always run late, that means you must be failing to account for something you always do. Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to arrive. Keep track of whether or not you actually do arrive early. You might find that leaving early gets you to places exactly on time.
lines.zh: 当你必须前往某个地方时，尽量提前15到30分钟到达。如果你总是迟到，这意味着你一定没有考虑到某件自己总会做的事情。通过给自己预留额外时间来提前应对这一点。记录自己是否真的提前到达。你可能会发现，提前出发反而能让你恰好准时到达目的地。

lines.en: Set two alarms. Set one alarm that lets you know it's time to drop what you're doing and a second alarm that means you need to walk out the door. Obey the alarms. As soon as the first alarm goes off, stop what you're doing. If it's something you'll be coming back to, like a project for work, make a note to remind yourself where you left off. Grab everything you need and make sure you know how to get where you're going. Aim to be out the door and on your way before the second alarm rings. This will only work if you take the alarms seriously, so make sure you react as soon as you hear them.
lines.zh: 设置两个闹钟。设置一个闹钟，提醒你该放下手头正在做的事情；再设置第二个闹钟，表示你必须出门了。遵守闹钟的提醒。第一个闹钟一响，就停止手头的事情。如果那是你之后还会继续做的事情，比如工作项目，就记下来提醒自己做到哪里。拿上所有需要的东西，并确保自己知道如何到达目的地。目标是在第二个闹钟响起之前出门上路。只有认真对待这两个闹钟，这种方法才会奏效，所以一听到闹钟响就要立即作出反应。

lines.en: Prepare for the day ahead. Have all of your notes and materials organized well in advance of each event, so that all you have to do is grab them and go when it's the actual day. If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before. Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.
lines.zh: 为第二天做好准备。提前整理好每项活动所需的全部笔记和材料，这样到了当天，你只需拿上它们就可以出发。如果早晨对你来说很难熬，就尽可能在前一晚做好准备。睡觉前，准备好第二天要穿的衣服，并收拾好包。

lines.en: Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings. It soon becomes unbearable to shift between one meeting and another without space in between. If you overschedule yourself, however, you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump. As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from, should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time. Calculate transit time between activities and then add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays.
lines.zh: 学会在任务和会议之间留出时间。在两个会议之间没有任何间隔地转换，很快就会让人难以忍受。然而，如果你的日程安排得过于紧凑，一遇到意外情况，你就会迟到。除了为你提供喘息空间外，这段时间还可以充当活动之间的缓冲；如果你在前一个会议上被耽搁了，就可以借用这段时间，从而仍能准时参加下一个会议。计算各项活动之间的交通时间，然后再增加10到30分钟，以应对意外延误。

lines.en: Do you think Bostonians put out the welcome mat? Do you find other cities to be more or less polite? Different cities have different feels for visitors. Some are friendly and open; some are formal and distant. Boston tends to seem hurried and sometimes a little rude. That's what some tourists have said. One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities. Take a close look next time you're in Boston, and here are some of the things you'll probably see: people smoking in the subway stations despite the frequent reminders not to do so; pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to do so, ignoring the cars; car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn and occasionally cursing at each other. Drivers who can't be bothered to find a place to park, but instead simply turn on their blinker and stop in the middle of the street.
lines.zh: 你认为波士顿人会铺上迎宾垫吗？你觉得其他城市的人更有礼貌，还是不那么有礼貌？不同的城市给游客的感觉各不相同。有些城市友好而开放，有些则拘谨而疏远。波士顿往往给人一种行色匆匆、有时还有些粗鲁的感觉。一些游客就是这么说的。一项研究发现，这里的人主动自愿帮助陌生人的意愿低于美国其他城市的居民。下次你在波士顿时，不妨仔细看看，你很可能会看到以下一些情景：尽管地铁站经常提醒人们不要吸烟，还是有人在那里吸烟；人行横道信号灯显示禁止通行时，行人仍然无视汽车继续行走；汽车司机超速行驶，大声按喇叭，偶尔还互相破口大骂。有些司机懒得找停车位，反而只是打开转向灯，把车停在马路中央。

lines.en: Sometimes Bostonians seem like they're just too busy to be polite. Why is their city like that? Former U.S. representative Chester Atkins says it's because the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered, and had little time for courtesy. That culture has carried down to the present day, he believes. Boston College professor Thomas O'Connor thinks a contributing factor is Boston's history as a city where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion and exclusion. That's given Boston a sense of clannishness and reserve, he thinks. The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says. People will begin a conversation with someone they know, but not with a stranger. Ralph Whitehead, a professor of journalism at the University of Massachusetts at Amherst, thinks it's because Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions. By being snobbish about manners, Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy, he says.
lines.zh: 有时波士顿人给人的感觉是，他们只是太忙了，顾不上讲礼貌。他们的城市为什么会这样？美国前众议员切斯特·阿特金斯说，这是因为那些清教徒开拓者本身就缺乏耐心、脾气暴躁，没有多少时间讲究礼节。他认为，这种文化一直延续到了今天。波士顿学院教授托马斯·奥康纳认为，另一个促成因素是波士顿的历史：每一批新来的移民都曾受到猜疑和排斥。他认为，这使波士顿形成了一种排外和矜持的气质。他说，陌生人主动向另一个陌生人打招呼，根本不属于当地文化的一部分。人们会与自己认识的人开始交谈，却不会与陌生人交谈。马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校新闻学教授拉尔夫·怀特黑德认为，这是因为波士顿上流社会曾利用礼仪来划分阶层。他说，波士顿那些讲究“正统礼仪”的人对礼仪表现得势利，从而使其他人开始鄙视礼节。

lines.en: Some say that's just the way Boston is and that the city will never change. Still, other cities with reputations for worse rudeness are trying hard to change their images. Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly. New York City is another. There, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate. If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well.
lines.zh: 有人说，波士顿就是这样，这座城市永远不会改变。不过，一些因粗鲁而声名更差的城市正在努力改变自己的形象。巴黎就是一个例子，那里的人们正在努力变得友好。纽约市是另一个例子。在那里，市政府正试图劝说地铁乘客更加体谅他人。如果那些城市都能付出努力，波士顿或许也应该这样做。

questions.stem: 【题目】 According to the speaker, what can we do to combat unexpected delays?
questions.stem_zh: 根据演讲者所说,我们可以做什么来应对意外延误?

analysis.定位: P5 Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings. As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from, should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time. 学会在各项任务和会议之间留出时间。这段时间除了给你余地,还在各项活动之间起到缓冲作用——万一前一场会议把你拖住了,可以从这段时间里挪用,让你仍能准时赶到下一场。
analysis.信号: 段首主张句+buffer 缓冲解释。答案信号是第五段段首的核心主张 Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings,其后用 acts as a buffer(充当缓冲)解释它正好能对付"被前一场拖住"的意外延误,与题干 combat unexpected delays 对上,据此锁定段首这句主张。
analysis.替换: leave time in between tasks and meetings↔Leave time in between activities.上位词概括替换 acts as a buffer between events↔Leave time in between activities.缓冲机制印证该做法
analysis.排除: A)原词陷阱Finish the prior task 30 minutes earlier. 盗用了末句的数字 add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays 里的"30 minutes":录音是说"为意外延误额外加留 10 到 30 分钟",并不是"把前一项任务提前 30 分钟完成",数字念到了、事却拼错了。 借用原文：add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays B)与原文相反Keep ourselves from hitting a bump. 盗用了 you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump 里的"hit a bump":录音是说"一旦把日程排太满,碰到颠簸就会迟到",讲的是过度排期的后果,而非教你"避免碰到颠簸";颠簸是无法避免的,要做的是留缓冲,选项把原意拧反了。 借用原文：you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump D)偷换概念Try to avoid possible hold-ups. 只是把题干目标"应对意外延误"换个说法重述一遍(avoid hold-ups),并未给出录音真正提出的可操作做法;且录音 should you be held up 把"被拖住"当成会发生、需用缓冲化解的事,而非教你"避免"它,这是空泛复述目标的陷阱。 借用原文：should you be held up

analysis.信号: study found 信号词。句首 One study found that 是题干 one study 的直接对应锚点，其后跟的就是研究结论，是答案句。
analysis.替换: less willing to volunteer to help strangers↔They are not as willing to help strangers.less=not as 同义改写

analysis.信号: he says 归属信号。这句以 he says 收尾，he 回指本段正在论述的 Thomas O'Connor，把观点准确归到他名下；其内容直接回答"陌生人打招呼"与文化的关系，是答案句。
analysis.替换: simply not part of the local culture↔It is not part of Boston's local culture.near-原句对应
analysis.排除: A)张冠李戴practiced by Boston's founding fathers 盗用了 the Puritan founding fathers，但那是 Chester Atkins 的说法、且讲的是性情急躁，与 O'Connor 谈"陌生人打招呼"无关，属张冠李戴。 借用原文：the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered B)原词陷阱not deemed exotic by Proper Bostonians 把 Proper Bostonians 这个原词拼到不存在的 exotic 上，Proper Bostonians 出自 Whitehead 谈"以礼仪划阶级"的论述，原文从无"是否异域风"之说，属原词陷阱。 借用原文：Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy C)张冠李戴adopted by Boston's upper class 盗用 Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions，那是 Whitehead 的说法、讲的是上层用礼仪划分阶级，并非 O'Connor 论"陌生人打招呼"，属张冠李戴。 借用原文：Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions

cloze.title: 2025年6月·第1套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: In her second year, Charlene Duong learned of the use of poisonous, synthetic pesticides on her college campus. Shocked but not surprised, she knew she had to do something. Along with a couple of classmates, Charlene did a quick web search and discovered a small but growing movement led by the organization, Herbicide-Free Campus (HFC), to rid college campuses of artificial herbicides(灭草剂). They were __(26)__ .
passages.zh: 大二时，Charlene Duong了解到她所在的大学校园使用有毒的合成农药。她既震惊又并不意外，知道自己必须采取行动。Charlene和两位同学一起快速进行了网络搜索，发现了一项由Herbicide-Free Campus（HFC）组织发起的、规模虽小但不断壮大的运动，旨在清除大学校园中的人工合成除草剂。他们对此产生了兴趣。

passages.en: Like many, Charlene experiences climate anxiety—a __(27)__ fear of a climate catastrophe—and was, at the time, looking for an __(28)__ . When she discovered the HFC movement, she said she felt she "had found a specific area to focus on that still fit into the larger picture of fighting for a healthier, safer, cleaner __(29)__ for all."
passages.zh: 和许多人一样，Charlene也经历着气候焦虑，即对气候灾难的长期恐惧；当时的她正在寻找一个宣泄这种情绪的出口。当她了解到HFC运动时，她说自己觉得“找到了一个可以专注于具体事务的领域，同时它仍然属于为所有人争取更健康、更安全、更清洁环境这一更大目标的一部分”。

passages.en: Toxic herbicide use in university land care is not unique. Most institutions of higher education rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers to achieve __(30)__ goals. Having a "beautiful" campus means green and perfectly maintained lawns along with flower beds and paved sidewalks. But these __(31)__ managed campuses can come at a cost: increased cancer risk, __(32)__ waterways, poisoned wildlife and lifeless soil.
passages.zh: 在大学校园的土地养护中使用有毒除草剂并非个例。大多数高等教育机构依靠合成农药和化肥来实现美观目标。拥有一个“漂亮”的校园，意味着有绿意盎然且维护得一丝不苟的草坪、花坛以及铺装的人行道。但以这种传统方式管理的校园可能要付出代价：癌症风险增加，水道受到污染，野生动物中毒，以及土壤失去生机。

passages.en: Pesticide use on college campuses also contributes to our global climate crisis. The use of chemicals to get rid of insects or unwanted plant life can increase indirect __(33)__ as they can include petroleum-based ingredients. Pesticide use also decreases the life in soil, __(34)__ the ability of soils to absorb carbon or retain water and thus reducing campuses' ability to recover quickly from climate-related extreme weather events like droughts and floods.
passages.zh: 大学校园使用农药也加剧了全球气候危机。使用化学品清除昆虫或不需要的植物可能会增加间接排放，因为这些化学品可能含有石油基成分。使用农药还会减少土壤中的生命，从而削弱土壤吸收碳或保持水分的能力，进而降低校园应对干旱和洪水等与气候相关的极端天气事件并迅速恢复的能力。

passages.en: Instead of using toxic chemicals, students working with HFC help out with __(35)__ the campus grounds.
passages.zh: 与使用有毒化学品不同，与HFC合作的学生会帮助清除校园里的杂草。

passages.en: "This work reminds me to be in the present moment as I play my role in reducing herbicide use and keeping my campus safe and healthy," says Charlene.
passages.zh: Charlene说：“这项工作提醒我活在当下，在减少除草剂使用、维护校园安全与健康的过程中发挥自己的作用。”

wordbank.gloss: 被污染的；污染（过去分词）
妨碍、阻碍（现在分词/动名词）
被深深吸引的、产生强烈兴趣的
（情感/精力）发泄/释放渠道；出口

rows.text: J) intrigued形容词
be 动词后作表语
发现新天地→产生兴趣 上文 discovered a small but growing movement 表明她们发现了一个新兴运动；They were __(26)__ 紧承其后，自然描述她们对这场运动**产生浓厚兴趣**的状态。be intrigued 是描述人被某事吸引的经典搭配。

A)aesthetic'她们是美学的'语义不通 aesthetic 修饰物的审美属性，不用于描述人的情绪反应，'They were aesthetic'语义荒谬。 C)contaminated'她们被污染了'语义不合 contaminated 修饰水/土等物质或抽象意义的'被污染的（思想）'，描述这群积极投身环保的学生，方向完全相反。 K)juvenile幼稚的与积极行动矛盾 juvenile 含贬义，会把这群有担当的大学生贬为'幼稚'，与全段她们果决行动的基调冲突。
B) chronic形容词
不定冠词与名词之间作定语
气候焦虑是长期慢性的 破折号后是对 climate anxiety 的同位解释。气候焦虑本质上是一种**长期、持续**的恐惧，chronic fear（慢性恐惧）是心理学常用搭配，正好刻画这种持续不消退的状态，与 'climate anxiety' 的本义对应。

A)aesthetic审美的不能修饰 fear aesthetic 指审美/美学的，与恐惧情绪无逻辑关系，搭配不成立。 C)contaminated被污染的不修饰情绪 contaminated 用于水、土壤等被污染的物质，不能修饰 fear 这种抽象情绪。 J)intrigued感兴趣的修饰人不修饰 fear intrigued 表'被深深吸引的'，主语通常是人，且与恐惧情绪在情感色彩上相反。 K)juvenile幼稚的与气候焦虑色彩冲突 juvenile 表'少年的/幼稚的'，带贬义，会把气候焦虑矮化为'孩子气的恐惧'，与下文积极行动的语调相悖。
L) outlet名词
不定冠词 an 后缺单数名词

气候焦虑需要情绪出口 上文 Charlene experiences climate anxiety—a __(27)__ fear of a climate catastrophe 说她有气候焦虑，下文 she felt she "had found a specific area to focus on" 表明她找到了可投入精力的具体领域——这正是焦虑情绪的**释放出口**（outlet）。look for an outlet 是描述情绪宣泄的固定搭配。
I)infringement侵权不是被'寻找'的对象 look for an infringement（寻找一项侵权行为）在语义上荒谬，且与 climate anxiety 的语境完全脱节。 N)vibrations辅音开头不能跟 an vibrations 以辅音 /v/ 开头，先被 an 拒之门外；且词义与气候焦虑无关。
F) environment名词
形容词串后缺名词中心词
三形容词指向'环境' healthier、safer、cleaner 是描述**生存环境**的高频搭配三件套，a healthier, safer, cleaner __(29)__ for all 整句承接上文 fighting for，正是为所有人争取一个更健康、安全、洁净的**环境**，与全文反对除草剂、保护校园生态的主旨完全吻合。

E)emissions排放物不能被'更健康'修饰 emissions 指废气排放物，搭配 healthier/safer/cleaner 在语义上矛盾——人们要的是减少排放，而不是'更健康的排放'。 I)infringement侵权与三形容词南辕北辙 infringement 指对权利的侵犯，是负面行为，无法用 healthier/safer/cleaner 来修饰，且与本文话题无关。 L)outlet释放渠道与'更健康'不搭 outlet 指情绪/精力的发泄出口，是个体层面的概念，不能用 healthier/safer/cleaner for all 这种宏观三连修饰。 N)vibrations振动与文章话题无关 vibrations 指物理振动，与气候、校园生态无关，纯粹凑数的干扰项。
A) aesthetic形容词
名词 goals 前作定语

美观目标对应下文绿色草坪 下文 Having a "beautiful" campus means green and perfectly maintained lawns along with flower beds and paved sidewalks 立刻解释了所谓 'goals' 就是把校园弄得**美观漂亮**——这正是 aesthetic（审美/美观）目标。命题人用引号 "beautiful" 直接回扣 aesthetic。
C)contaminated被污染的目标语义颠倒 contaminated goals（被污染的目标）语义不通；高校追求的不可能是'被污染'目标，方向反了。 K)juvenile幼稚目标与高校追求不符 juvenile goals 含贬义，高校公开追求'幼稚目标'语义荒诞，与下文美观校园语境无关。
D) conventionally副词
形容词 managed 前作状语

传统方式=合成农药管理 上文 Most institutions of higher education rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers 说大多数高校沿用合成农药——这正是**传统/常规**管理方式；these __(31)__ managed campuses 中的 these 回指前句，因此填 conventionally（按传统方式）正好呼应。
H)incidentally顺便地与代价主句无关 incidentally 意为'顺便提一句、偶然地'，常作插入语，无法刻画'校园被怎样管理'的方式；与下文 'come at a cost' 的因果论证脱节。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— 副词只剩两个，色彩不挑就翻车。31 题词性确定后只剩 conventionally 和 incidentally 两选一。考生若只看词性、不回头读上文 Most institutions of higher education rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers 的'常规手段'铺垫，就可能误选 incidentally。防坑：副词空二选一时，必回上文找语义铺垫。
C) contaminated形容词
名词 waterways 前作定语
并列同义堆叠负面后果 increased cancer risk, __(32)__ waterways, poisoned wildlife and lifeless soil 是命题人列出的四宗罪：增加癌症风险、__水道、毒害野生动物、贫瘠土壤。waterways 与化学品代价最自然的搭配就是 contaminated（被污染的），与 poisoned/lifeless 一同构成负面后果链。
K)juvenile幼稚的水道语义不通 juvenile waterways（幼稚的水道）搭配不成立，且不属于负面后果范畴。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— 形容词色彩一错全错。32 题在并列负面后果 poisoned wildlife、lifeless soil 之间，考生若只挑形容词词性不察色彩，可能把 juvenile 硬塞进去。防坑：并列项前的修饰词必须与左右邻居在感情色彩上一致。
E) emissions名词
形容词后作宾语缺名词复数

石油成分对应温室气体排放 as they can include petroleum-based ingredients 明示这些化学品含石油基成分，正是温室气体排放（emissions）的来源；上文 Pesticide use on college campuses also contributes to our global climate crisis 也铺垫了气候话题，indirect emissions 即'间接排放'是气候议题的标准术语。

I)infringement侵权与石油成分无逻辑链 infringement 指权利侵犯，无法解释为何'含石油成分'会导致它增加，与气候危机话题完全无关。 L)outlet发泄渠道与排放概念错位 outlet 虽有'出口'义，但常指情感/能量的发泄渠道或电源插座，不用于描述温室气体的间接产生，与 petroleum-based ingredients 接不上。 N)vibrations振动与石油成分无关 vibrations 指物理振动，与气候危机、石油成分无任何因果链。
G) hampering动词
并列分词作伴随状语
削弱土壤功能=妨碍其能力 decreases the life in soil, __(34)__ the ability of soils to absorb carbon or retain water，主句说减少土壤生命，分词层进一步说**妨碍**土壤吸收碳/保水的能力；hampering（妨碍）与 reducing（减少）在 and 前后形成同义递进，语义、形态都对齐。
M)rotating旋转土壤能力语义不通 rotating the ability of soils（旋转土壤能力）搭配不成立；rotating 通常用于轮作（rotating crops）等，与本句负面后果链脱节。
O) weeding动词
with 后接动名词作宾语
替代农药=人工除草 上文 Instead of using toxic chemicals 明示是有毒化学品的**替代方案**——既然不喷除草剂，那学生帮忙做的就是**人工除草**（weeding）。weed the campus grounds（给校园场地除草）也是该词的典型搭配。
G)hampering妨碍校园场地语义颠倒 hampering the campus grounds（妨碍校园场地）语义荒谬，且学生'帮忙'不可能是'妨碍'，与 help out 的色彩反向。 M)rotating轮作场地与替代农药无关 rotating the campus grounds（旋转/轮换校园场地）语义牵强，与上文'不用化学药品'的对照逻辑接不上。

longreading.title: 2025年6月·第1套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) Librarians know the value of their community services, and their patrons appreciate their importance as well. But in an increasingly digital world, we see the role of libraries as community and cultural centers at times undervalued. When shrinking municipal budgets combine with the nonstop technological revolution, public library services that focus on building communities face-to-face, inspiring and educating patrons about art, literature, and music, and helping patrons engage in civil discourse can seem old-fashioned. But it is precisely those shrinking budgets and the assault of technologically mediated life that make public libraries' cultural and community offerings more important than ever.
passages.zh: 图书馆员了解其社区服务的价值，读者也同样认可这些服务的重要性。然而，在一个日益数字化的世界里，我们有时会看到图书馆作为社区和文化中心的作用被低估。当不断缩减的市政预算与永不停息的技术革命相互叠加时，那些致力于面对面建设社区、启发和教育读者了解艺术、文学和音乐，并帮助读者参与文明对话的公共图书馆服务，似乎会显得过时。但恰恰是这些不断缩减的预算以及技术媒介化生活的冲击，使公共图书馆提供的文化和社区服务比以往任何时候都更加重要。

passages.en: B) Many people point out the value public libraries bring to their communities. More than just books and banks of computers, libraries are still places where individuals gather to explore, interact, and imagine. Some of the specific ways in which libraries add value to our communities and serve as cultural centers for our patrons are community builders, centers for the arts, and champions of youth. Libraries serve in these capacities and are more than just about information.
passages.zh: 许多人指出，公共图书馆为所在社区带来了价值。图书馆不仅仅是存放书籍和摆放成排电脑的地方，它们仍然是人们聚集在一起探索、互动和想象的场所。图书馆为社区增值并作为读者文化中心发挥作用的具体方式包括建设社区、支持艺术以及关爱青少年。图书馆承担着这些职能，其意义远不只是提供信息。

passages.en: C) As community builders libraries are engaged in incredible work. From tiny public libraries to huge city institutions with multiple branches, libraries across the United States are building community and supporting local culture in exciting ways. These are inspiring and hopefully will encourage librarians interested in community services and cultural outreach to make connections with each other, share ideas, and build partnerships. Supporters of libraries as community builders claim that unless you are out there changing neighborhoods, you are not completing the work you are to do. Strengthening neighborhoods and championing the cultural lives of communities are big responsibilities.
passages.zh: 作为社区建设者，图书馆正在开展令人瞩目的工作。从微型公共图书馆到拥有多个分馆的大型城市机构，美国各地的图书馆都在以令人振奋的方式建设社区、支持地方文化。这些实践令人深受鼓舞，也希望能够促使那些对社区服务和文化推广感兴趣的图书馆员彼此建立联系、分享想法并开展合作。支持图书馆作为社区建设者的人认为，除非你真正走进社区、改变街区，否则就没有完成自己应尽的工作。加强街区建设、推动社区文化生活发展，是重大的责任。

passages.en: D) Place-based economic development stresses the importance of offering attractive, functional, and community-based places, such as libraries, in town squares and depressed neighborhoods. Like a major department store in a mall, libraries attract large numbers of people, creating economic opportunities for numerous businesses and organizations in the surrounding area. Large cities, medium-sized ones, and even small towns have successfully transformed their libraries into the hubs(枢纽) of vibrant neighborhoods.
passages.zh: 基于地方的经济发展强调，在城镇广场和经济衰退的街区提供具有吸引力、功能完善且以社区为基础的场所，例如图书馆，具有重要意义。图书馆就像购物中心里的大型百货商店一样，能够吸引大量人流，为周边众多企业和组织创造经济机会。大城市、中等城市，甚至小城镇，都成功地将图书馆改造成充满活力的街区枢纽。

passages.en: E) As key municipal agencies, and focal points for community education, libraries are major players in creating livable, environmentally friendly cities and towns. The Urban Libraries Council released a report detailing the unique ways in which libraries can further sustainability at the local level. Beyond ensuring that library construction projects consider environmental impact, libraries can take a lead in supporting local foods and craftsmen, like the Peabody Institute Library's partnering with local businesses to pioneer a farmers' market in their courtyard, or the Richmond Public Library's seed lending library which "nurtures locally-adapted plant varieties, and fosters community resilience(韧性), self-reliance and a culture of sharing."
passages.zh: 作为重要的市政机构和社区教育的焦点，图书馆是建设宜居、环保的城市和城镇的重要参与者。城市图书馆委员会发布了一份报告，详细说明了图书馆能够在地方层面进一步推动可持续发展的独特方式。除了确保图书馆建设项目考虑环境影响之外，图书馆还可以带头支持本地食品和手工艺者，例如皮博迪学院图书馆与当地企业合作，在其庭院中率先创办农贸市场；又如里士满公共图书馆的种子借阅图书馆，它“培育适应本地环境的植物品种，增强社区韧性、自立能力以及共享文化”。

passages.en: F) Archives preserve historic artifacts, oral histories, digital history projects, and scholarly writings relevant to the community, including minority groups. Communities lucky enough to have archivists have a great advantage when it comes to organizing historical records and artifacts. An organized archive is a place where people can research their ancestry and immigration history, do environmental research, and more. An archivist is an advocate for preservation who, among other things, coordinates the restoration of maps and paintings, the digitization of vital records, and the creation of oral history projects. With projects like the Massachussets Memories Road Show and the Veterans History Project, evidence of the importance of archives is everywhere.
passages.zh: 档案馆保存与社区相关的历史文物、口述历史、数字历史项目和学术著作，其中也包括与少数群体有关的资料。拥有档案工作人员的社区，在整理历史记录和文物方面具有很大优势。一个组织完善的档案馆是人们研究祖先和移民历史、开展环境研究等活动的场所。档案工作人员是保存工作的倡导者，除其他工作外，还负责协调地图和绘画作品的修复、重要记录的数字化以及口述历史项目的创建。Massachussets Memories Road Show 和 Veterans History Project 等项目随处可见，它们都证明了档案馆的重要性。

passages.en: G) In the words of Robert Putnam, "People may go to the library looking mainly for information, but they find each other there." New moms connect at baby story-times; elderly people, often facing difficult life transitions, attend events and find that they make new friends; teenagers meet up in libraries' teen spaces after school; and readers discuss current events in the periodicals room. In libraries, community-building connections are happening all the time.
passages.zh: 用罗伯特·帕特南的话说：“人们去图书馆主要可能是为了寻找信息，但他们在那里找到了彼此。”新手妈妈们在婴儿故事时间相互联系；老年人常常面临艰难的人生转折，他们参加活动并发现自己结交了新朋友；青少年放学后在图书馆的青少年空间碰面；读者则在期刊阅览室讨论时事。在图书馆里，建设社区的联系时时刻刻都在发生。

passages.en: H) As Keith Richards said, "The public library is the great equalizer." Despite the rising costs of concert and theater tickets, public library events (including concerts, author visits, and gallery displays) are often offered free of charge, enabling people of any income level to attend. In addition, library book groups allow people to explore and discuss the literary arts, and the Great Stories Club introduces at-risk youth to literature. The best part: it's all free and open to the public.
passages.zh: 正如基思·理查兹所说：“公共图书馆是伟大的平等izador。”尽管音乐会和戏剧演出的门票价格不断上涨，公共图书馆举办的活动，包括音乐会、作家见面会和画廊展览，通常都免费提供，使任何收入水平的人都能够参加。此外，图书馆读书会让人们能够探讨和讨论文学艺术，而 Great Stories Club 则将文学介绍给处境危险的青少年。最重要的是：这一切都免费向公众开放。

passages.en: I) In a time when education is increasingly expensive, public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status. Offered by libraries across the country, American Library Association's Let's Talk about It programs are wonderful examples of scholar-facilitated learning opportunities in libraries. In addition, many libraries present classes and discussion programs, and some even provide online continuing education courses such as the Universal Class database.
passages.zh: 在教育成本日益高昂的时代，公共图书馆为所有人免费提供信息和受教育的机会，不论其社会经济地位如何。美国图书馆协会在全国各地的图书馆开展的“Let's Talk about It”项目，就是由学者引导的图书馆学习机会的优秀范例。此外，许多图书馆还开设课程和讨论项目，有些甚至通过 Universal Class 数据库提供在线继续教育课程。

passages.en: J) Librarians know that patrons aren't just information consumers, they're information producers. Patrons use the library to gain knowledge in order to create their own new and independent works. Increasing numbers of libraries provide spaces and services that meet the needs of people who want to learn how to edit Wikipedia, set up blogs or podcasts, create their own magazines, and so much more. Many libraries offer art or writing workshops and groups, and some provide music practice rooms for patrons. Programs like ImaginOn in Charlotte, North Carolina, provide exciting models that take community partnership, creativity, and creation to a new level.
passages.zh: 图书馆员知道，读者不仅是信息消费者，也是信息生产者。读者利用图书馆获取知识，以创作属于自己的新作品和独立作品。越来越多的图书馆提供空间和服务，以满足那些希望学习编辑维基百科、创建博客或播客、制作自己的杂志以及开展更多活动的人们的需要。许多图书馆开设艺术或写作工作坊和小组，有些还为读者提供音乐练习室。北卡罗来纳州夏洛特市的 ImaginOn 等项目提供了令人振奋的范例，将社区合作、创造力和创作提升到了新的水平。

passages.en: K) The decline of civil discourse stems in part from the fact that it is so easy for people to watch news about, buy products from, and engage—in both the virtual and real worlds—only with those of similar backgrounds and ideologies. Public libraries, through such programs as The Human Library and Socrates Café, can help build small communities of difference that encourage people to interact with and learn from each other through dialogue. By both actively promoting civil discourse through these programs, and modeling and upholding the principles of free inquiry and expression for all, libraries help individuals rediscover the importance of and increased need for civil discourse in American life.
passages.zh: 文明对话的衰落部分源于这样一个事实：人们很容易只观看与自己背景和意识形态相似者制作的新闻，只购买他们提供的产品，并只与他们互动，无论是在虚拟世界还是现实世界中。公共图书馆通过 The Human Library 和 Socrates Café 等项目，能够帮助建设由不同背景的人组成的小型社区，鼓励人们通过对话彼此互动并相互学习。图书馆既通过这些项目积极促进文明对话，又为所有人示范并维护自由探究和自由表达的原则，从而帮助个人重新发现文明对话在美国生活中的重要性以及日益增长的需求。

passages.en: L) Free tutoring, homework help programs, and summer reading programs for kids and teens help bridge the economic divide that impacts students' academic performance. The cost of hiring a private tutor is well beyond what many library patrons can afford, so libraries offer homework help and tutoring online, by phone, in person, and even through social media and homework apps. Annual summer reading programs also have a positive impact on student performance and, according to a 2010 study conducted by Dominican University's Graduate School of Library and Information Science, students' reading skills get a boost from these popular nationwide events.
passages.zh: 免费的辅导、作业帮助项目以及面向儿童和青少年的暑期阅读项目，有助于弥合影响学生学业表现的经济差距。聘请私人家教的费用远远超出许多图书馆读者的承受能力，因此图书馆通过网络、电话、面对面方式，甚至借助社交媒体和作业应用程序，提供作业帮助和辅导。每年举办的暑期阅读项目也会对学生的表现产生积极影响；根据多米尼加大学图书馆与信息科学研究生院于2010年开展的一项研究，学生的阅读技能会因这些在全国各地广受欢迎的活动而得到提高。

passages.en: M) Through library collections, programs, and physical spaces, children learn to share, to be engaged in their communities, to participate in the arts, and to explore their immediate world and the world at large. There are surely endless examples of innovative library services for children, including the Middle Country Public Library's Nature Explorium, which engages children in learning about the natural world.
passages.zh: 通过图书馆的馆藏、项目和实体空间，儿童学会分享，积极参与社区，参加艺术活动，并探索身边的世界和更广阔的世界。图书馆为儿童提供的创新服务例子无疑数不胜数，其中包括 Middle Country Public Library 的 Nature Explorium，该项目让儿童参与了解自然世界的学习活动。

passages.en: N) These examples are just a few of the many amazing things that public libraries around the United States (and the world) are doing to build and maintain strong community connections. We encourage you to try some of these ideas in your own libraries, and we hope that these ideas will help you be better able to convince your community leaders of the important role that public libraries play in communities large and small.
passages.zh: 这些例子只是美国各地乃至全世界公共图书馆为建立和维护牢固的社区联系所开展的众多精彩工作中的一小部分。我们鼓励你们在自己的图书馆尝试其中的一些做法，也希望这些想法能够帮助你们更好地说服社区领导者认识到公共图书馆在大大小小的社区中所发挥的重要作用。

statements.en: People going to the library in search of information can build connections with each other there.
statements.zh: 去图书馆寻找信息的人可以在那里彼此建立联系。

analysis.锚点: 找信息却建立彼此联系
analysis.定位: G 段 In the words of Robert Putnam, "People may go to the library looking mainly for information, but they find each other there." 用罗伯特·普特南的话说："人们去图书馆主要是为了寻找信息，但他们在那里彼此相遇。"
analysis.改写: People going to the library in search of information↔People may go to the library looking mainly for information "寻找信息"原样同义 can build connections with each other there↔they find each other there "找到彼此"="建立连接"

statements.en: According to advocates of libraries as community builders, librarians are not doing their job well if they do not change their communities.
statements.zh: 根据倡导图书馆作为社区建设者的人的观点,如果图书馆员不改变他们的社区,就没有做好本职工作。

analysis.锚点: 倡导者 + 不改变社区即未尽职
analysis.定位: C 段 Supporters of libraries as community builders claim that unless you are out there changing neighborhoods, you are not completing the work you are to do. 支持图书馆作为社区建设者的倡导者声称：除非你走出去改变所在社区，否则你就没有完成你该做的工作。
analysis.改写: advocates of libraries as community builders↔Supporters of libraries as community builders advocates ↔ Supporters 同义 librarians are not doing their job well if they do not change their communities↔unless you are out there changing neighborhoods, you are not completing the work you are to do unless 双否定 ↔ if not 肯定条件
analysis.辨邻: B B 段虽然出现 community builders 这个标签，但没有任何"不改变社区就没做好工作"的主张，缺第二层指纹。 Some of the specific ways in which libraries add value to our communities and serve as cultural centers for our patrons are community builders, centers for the arts, and champions of youth.

statements.en: With the costs of education continually rising, public libraries remain places where all people can have access to education.
statements.zh: 随着教育成本不断上升,公共图书馆仍然是所有人都能获得教育的场所。

analysis.锚点: 教育成本上升 + 人人可获取教育
analysis.定位: I 段 In a time when education is increasingly expensive, public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status. 在教育越来越昂贵的时代，公共图书馆免费向所有人提供信息与教育机会，无论其社会经济地位如何。
analysis.改写: With the costs of education continually rising↔In a time when education is increasingly expensive "成本上升"="越来越贵"名词化重构 public libraries remain places where all people can have access to education↔public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status "人人有教育机会"原样同义
analysis.辨邻: H H 段谈的是 concerts, author visits, and gallery displays 这种文化活动免费，不是 education；少了"教育越来越贵"的前提，整句对不上。 public library events (including concerts, author visits, and gallery displays) are often offered free of charge, enabling people of any income level to attend L L 段聚焦 students 与 tutoring, homework help programs, and summer reading programs，未提及"教育成本不断上升"作为整体前提，且适用人群是学生不是所有人。 Free tutoring, homework help programs, and summer reading programs for kids and teens help bridge the economic divide that impacts students' academic performance

statements.en: Libraries draw large crowds, thus creating lots of business opportunities in neighboring areas.
statements.zh: 图书馆吸引大量人群,从而在周边地区创造了许多商业机会。

analysis.锚点: 吸引人流 + 周边商机
analysis.定位: D 段 Like a major department store in a mall, libraries attract large numbers of people, creating economic opportunities for numerous businesses and organizations in the surrounding area. 就像商场里的主力百货公司一样，图书馆吸引大量人流，为周边的众多企业和机构创造经济机会。
analysis.改写: Libraries draw large crowds↔libraries attract large numbers of people draw=attract，crowds=large numbers of people creating lots of business opportunities in neighboring areas↔creating economic opportunities for numerous businesses and organizations in the surrounding area business=economic for businesses，neighboring=surrounding

statements.en: With the world more and more digitalized, people sometimes underestimate the role of libraries as community and cultural centers.
statements.zh: 随着世界越来越数字化,人们有时会低估图书馆作为社区和文化中心的作用。

analysis.锚点: 世界数字化 + 角色被低估
analysis.定位: A 段 But in an increasingly digital world, we see the role of libraries as community and cultural centers at times undervalued. 但是，在一个日益数字化的世界里，我们有时会看到图书馆作为社区与文化中心的角色被低估。
analysis.改写: With the world more and more digitalized↔in an increasingly digital world "日益数字化"原样同义 people sometimes underestimate the role of libraries as community and cultural centers↔we see the role of libraries as community and cultural centers at times undervalued underestimate=undervalued，sometimes=at times

statements.en: Various programs organized by public libraries for children and adolescents help narrow the gap between students from varying economic backgrounds.
statements.zh: 公共图书馆为儿童和青少年组织的各种项目有助于缩小来自不同经济背景的学生之间的差距。

analysis.锚点: 面向儿童青少年的项目 + 缩小经济差距
analysis.定位: L 段 Free tutoring, homework help programs, and summer reading programs for kids and teens help bridge the economic divide that impacts students' academic performance. 面向少年儿童的免费辅导、作业辅导项目以及暑期阅读项目，帮助弥合那条影响学生学业表现的经济鸿沟。
analysis.改写: Various programs organized by public libraries for children and adolescents↔Free tutoring, homework help programs, and summer reading programs for kids and teens 上位词 programs 总括多个具体项目 narrow the gap between students from varying economic backgrounds↔bridge the economic divide that impacts students' academic performance narrow=bridge，gap=divide
analysis.辨邻: M M 段聚焦 children learn to share, to be engaged in their communities, to participate in the arts，与题干"缩小经济差距"无对应。 Through library collections, programs, and physical spaces, children learn to share, to be engaged in their communities, to participate in the arts, and to explore their immediate world and the world at large.

statements.en: In an organized archive, people can do research on their family history and find out how their ancestors came to settle in the new land.
statements.zh: 在有组织的档案馆中,人们可以研究自己的家族史,了解他们的祖先是如何来到新大陆定居的。

analysis.锚点: 档案 + 家族史 + 祖辈如何来到新土地
analysis.定位: F 段 An organized archive is a place where people can research their ancestry and immigration history, do environmental research, and more. 一个组织有序的档案馆，是人们可以研究自己的祖辈血统与移民史、做环境研究等的地方。
analysis.改写: In an organized archive↔An organized archive is a place 原样复现 people can do research on their family history↔people can research their ancestry family history=ancestry find out how their ancestors came to settle in the new land↔immigration history "移民史"= 祖辈如何来到新土地

statements.en: Public libraries organize cultural events, often allowing people of different income levels to attend free of charge.
statements.zh: 公共图书馆组织文化活动,通常允许不同收入水平的人免费参加。

analysis.锚点: 文化活动 + 不同收入层次免费参与
analysis.定位: H 段 Despite the rising costs of concert and theater tickets, public library events (including concerts, author visits, and gallery displays) are often offered free of charge, enabling people of any income level to attend. 尽管音乐会和剧院门票越来越贵，公共图书馆举办的活动（包括音乐会、作家见面会和画廊展览）却常常免费提供，让任何收入水平的人都能参加。
analysis.改写: Public libraries organize cultural events↔public library events (including concerts, author visits, and gallery displays) cultural events 上位概括 allowing people of different income levels to attend free of charge↔offered free of charge, enabling people of any income level to attend allowing=enabling，different=any income level
analysis.辨邻: I I 段谈的是 provide information and educational opportunities free for all people，与题干 cultural events 对象不一致。 public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status

statements.en: Besides being an information provider, the library performs many other important services for the community.
statements.zh: 除了作为信息提供者之外,图书馆还为社区提供许多其他重要服务。

analysis.锚点: 信息提供者之外的多重服务
analysis.定位: B 段 More than just books and banks of computers, libraries are still places where individuals gather to explore, interact, and imagine. 图书馆不仅是书籍与成排电脑的所在，仍是人们聚集起来探索、互动与想象的地方。
analysis.改写: Besides being an information provider↔More than just books and banks of computers besides=more than just，两种总览结构互替 the library performs many other important services for the community↔Libraries serve in these capacities and are more than just about information performs many other services=serve in these capacities + more than information
analysis.辨邻: A A 段 we see the role of libraries as community and cultural centers at times undervalued 谈的是评价（低估），而非"列举信息以外的多种服务"。 public library services that focus on building communities face-to-face, inspiring and educating patrons about art, literature, and music, and helping patrons engage in civil discourse can seem old-fashioned N N 段 These examples are just a few of the many amazing things that public libraries around the United States (and the world) are doing to build and maintain strong community connections 落点是"鼓励复制 + 说服领导"，与题干的总览主张不一致。 We encourage you to try some of these ideas in your own libraries, and we hope that these ideas will help you be better able to convince your community leaders of the important role that public libraries play in communities large and small.

statements.en: Public libraries can help build small communities of people with different backgrounds and ideologies.
statements.zh: 公共图书馆可以帮助建立由不同背景和意识形态的人组成的小型社区。

analysis.锚点: 不同背景与意识形态的小型社区
analysis.定位: K 段 Public libraries, through such programs as The Human Library and Socrates Café, can help build small communities of difference that encourage people to interact with and learn from each other through dialogue. 公共图书馆通过 The Human Library 和 Socrates Café 等项目，能够帮助构建由差异组成的小型社区，鼓励人们通过对话相互交流、相互学习。
analysis.改写: build small communities of people with different backgrounds and ideologies↔build small communities of difference of difference 展开为 of people with different ... Public libraries can help↔Public libraries, through such programs as The Human Library and Socrates Café, can help 原样复现
analysis.辨邻: G G 段 community-building connections are happening all the time 强调的是"找信息 → 找到彼此"的反差，与题干"不同背景与意识形态"的限定不一致。 New moms connect at baby story-times; elderly people, often facing difficult life transitions, attend events and find that they make new friends; teenagers meet up in libraries' teen spaces after school; and readers discuss current events in the periodicals room.

reading1.title: 2025年6月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 1 篇 · 46–50 题答案与解析

passages.en: Nationally, one in six children miss 15 or more days of school in a year. Education officials have deplored all this missed instruction.
passages.zh: 从全国范围来看，每六名儿童中就有一名每年缺课15天或以上。教育官员对如此大量的教学缺失表示了强烈不满。

passages.en: These chronically absent students suffer academically because of all the classroom instruction they miss out on. In 2015, the U.S. secretary of education responded to this crisis, urging communities to support every student to attend every day and be successful in school. His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement.
passages.zh: 这些长期缺课的学生由于错过了大量课堂教学，在学业上受到影响。2015年，美国教育部长回应了这一危机，敦促各社区支持每一名学生每天到校，并在学校取得成功。他在一封公开信中指出，无论出于何种原因——获准缺勤或未经批准缺勤——每年缺课达到在校日的10%，都是学业成绩低下的主要原因。

passages.en: Worrying about whether children attend school makes sense. After all, if students don't show up, teachers can't teach them.
passages.zh: 担心儿童是否到校上课是有道理的。毕竟，如果学生不来，教师就无法教他们。

passages.en: But what if America's attendance crisis is about much more than students missing class? What if, instead, it is a reflection of family and community crises these students face—such as being ejected from the family apartment, fearing for their safety in their neighborhood or suffering an illness?
passages.zh: 但是，如果美国的出勤危机远不只是学生缺课呢？如果它实际上反映的是这些学生所面临的家庭和社区危机呢？例如，他们被赶出家庭公寓、担心所在社区的人身安全，或正在遭受疾病困扰。

passages.en: As social scientists we investigated how excused and unexcused absences relate to children's academic achievement.
passages.zh: 作为社会科学家，我们研究了获准缺勤和未经批准缺勤与儿童学业成绩之间的关系。

passages.en: We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning. In fact, children with no unexcused absences—but 15 to 18 excused absences—have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences.
passages.zh: 我们发现，家长批准的缺勤对儿童的学习几乎没有不良影响。事实上，那些没有未经批准缺勤、但有15至18次获准缺勤的儿童，其考试成绩与没有缺勤记录的同龄人相同。

passages.en: Meanwhile, the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none.
passages.zh: 与此同时，即使只有一次未经批准缺勤的普通儿童，其学业表现也远不如没有未经批准缺勤的同龄人。

passages.en: We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of-school challenges affect children's academic progress.
passages.zh: 我们认为，未经批准缺勤是儿童和家庭面临诸多挑战的强烈信号，其中包括经济困难和医疗困境。未经批准缺勤可以有力地反映出那些发生在校外的挑战如何影响儿童的学业进步。

passages.en: Our evidence suggests unexcused absences are problematic, but for a different reason than people often think. Absence from school, and especially unexcused absence, matters mainly as a signal of many crises children and their families may be facing. It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction.
passages.zh: 我们的证据表明，未经批准缺勤确实存在问题，但原因不同于人们通常所认为的那样。缺课，尤其是未经批准缺勤，主要是儿童及其家庭可能正在面临诸多危机的一种信号。与由于错过教学而导致学生成绩下降相比，缺课作为成绩下降原因的重要性较低。

passages.en: How we choose to think of school absences matters for educational policy. School attendance policies typically hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss, regardless of whether they were excused or unexcused absences.
passages.zh: 我们如何看待学生缺课，会影响教育政策的制定。学校出勤政策通常会让学校和家庭对儿童缺课的天数负责，而不论这些缺勤属于获准缺勤还是未经批准缺勤。

passages.en: These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically because they are missing classroom instruction. They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. We find neither to be the case.
passages.zh: 这些政策认为，学生无论出于何种原因缺课，都会因为错过课堂教学而在学业上受到损害。它们还认为，学校能够通过减少学生缺勤来进行有效干预。我们发现，事实并非如此。

passages.en: As a result, these attendance policies end up disproportionately punishing families dealing with out-of-school crises in their lives and pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often.
passages.zh: 因此，这些出勤政策最终会对那些正在应对生活中校外危机的家庭施加不成比例的惩罚，并向为这些家庭提供服务的学校施压，要求它们让学生更加频繁地到校。

passages.en: We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.
passages.zh: 相反，我们建议将学生未经批准缺勤作为一种信号，把资源引导给最需要帮助的儿童和家庭。

questions.stem: What does the U.S. secretary of education say in his open letter?
questions.stem_zh: 美国教育部长在他的公开信中说了什么?

options.text: It is of vital importance to respond promptly to the school absence crisis.
options.zh: 及时应对学校缺勤危机至关重要。

options.text: The academic performance of chronically absent students is deplorable.
options.zh: 长期缺勤学生的学业表现令人担忧。

options.text: Low academic achievement is mainly attributed to school absences.
options.zh: 学业成绩低下主要归因于学校缺勤。

options.text: The effect of school absences on American education is worrisome.
options.zh: 学校缺勤对美国教育的影响令人担忧。

questions.判型: What does the U.S. secretary of education say in his open letter? 问的是某人具体说的内容，答案就在原文某句话里，不需推断。
questions.拆句: 结构是 What does the U.S. secretary of education say in his open letter?——典型 what 引导的特殊疑问句，主语 the U.S. secretary of education，谓语 say，介词短语 in his open letter 限定 say 的发生场景；无从句、无否定、无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement. 他的公开信指出，一年缺课 10%——无论是否有故——是低学业成就的一个主要原因。

locate.en: His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement.
locate.zh: 他的公开信指出，一年缺课 10%——无论是否有故——是低学业成就的一个主要原因。

option_analysis.note: 公开信里没有任何关于 "必须迅速回应" 的话——urging communities to support every student 是劝学校社区支持学生出勤，不是对 respond promptly 的呼吁；A 项把作者（urging）的动作改写成信件内容，且加了原文没有的 "vital importance / promptly" 程度词。
deplored 在原文里描述的是 Education officials 对 "all this missed instruction" 的态度，B 项把它偷换成了 "chronically absent students 的 academic performance is deplorable"——主语从 "缺课现象" 偷换成 "学生的学业表现"，evaluatee 错位。
C 项把 missing 10% of school days … is a primary cause of low academic achievement 的主动因果倒装为 "低学业主要归因于缺课" 的被动因果，与预判 "缺课是学业差的主因" 完全吻合。

pairs.orig: missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason
is a primary cause of low academic achievement
pairs.opt: Low academic achievement is mainly attributed to

option_analysis.note: 公开信原文用 primary cause 的客观因果定性，并未对 "school absences 对美国教育的影响" 作 worrisome 这种情感色彩评价——D 项把 Worrying 段的句首词搬到这里，但那是作者对 "担心缺勤" 的转述，并非教育部长公开信的内容。

questions.stem: What do the authors find about school absences?
questions.stem_zh: 作者对学校缺勤有什么发现?

options.text: Excused school absences have little impact on children's learning.
options.zh: 请假缺勤对儿童学习影响很小。

options.text: There is little difference between unexcused and excused absences.
options.zh: 无故缺勤和请假缺勤之间几乎没有差别。

options.text: Excused absences lead to comparatively better school performance.
options.zh: 请假缺勤导致相对更好的学业表现。

options.text: Unexcused absences are a big challenge to both schools and families.
options.zh: 无故缺勤对学校和家庭都是一个巨大挑战。

questions.判型: What do the authors find about school absences? 问的是作者的客观发现，原文必有对应陈述句，不属于推断。
questions.拆句: 结构是 What do the authors find about school absences?——What 作 find 的宾语，主语 the authors，介词短语 about school absences 限定 find 的话题范围；句法简单，没有陷阱。
questions.定位: P6 We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning. 我们发现，由家长请假的 excused absences 对孩子的学习几乎没有伤害。

locate.en: We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning.
locate.zh: 我们发现，由家长请假的 excused absences 对孩子的学习几乎没有伤害。

option_analysis.note: A 项是 P6 第一句的字面同义改写——主语 excused absences、谓语 do little to harm 全部一一对应，无任何添加或扭曲，与预判完全吻合。

pairs.orig: do little to harm children's learning
pairs.opt: have little impact on children's learning

option_analysis.note: 原文 the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none 明确指出 unexcused 与 excused 差异很大——B 项 little difference 与原文 much worse 直接相反。
原文只说 excused absences do little to harm、有 excused 缺勤的孩子 have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences——是 "equal to"（相当），不是 comparatively better（相对更好）。"持平" 被悄悄抬升为 "更好"。
Unexcused absences are a big challenge to both schools and families 谈的是 unexcused 对学校和家庭构成挑战——题干 Q47 问的是 "authors 关于 school absences 的发现"，作者的核心发现是 excused 不损学（P6），而非 unexcused 对学校家庭有多挑战。话题偏离。

questions.stem: What do the authors believe concerning unexcused school absences?
questions.stem_zh: 作者对无故缺勤持什么看法?

options.text: They are likely to cause a decrease in students' academic achievements due to missed instruction.
options.zh: 由于错过了教学,它们可能导致学生学业成绩下降。

options.text: They point directly to many of the out-of-school challenges confronting children and their families.
options.zh: 它们直接指向儿童及其家庭面临的许多校外挑战。

options.text: They are matters the American government typically ignores when formulating educational policies.
options.zh: 在制定教育政策时,美国政府通常会忽视这些问题。

options.text: They give a clear signal to children and their families of the crises they are likely to face in the future.
options.zh: 它们向儿童及其家庭发出了未来可能面临危机的明确信号。

questions.判型: What do the authors believe concerning unexcused school absences? 问的是作者已经明说的观点，原文有原句，属于细节题。
questions.拆句: 结构是 What do the authors believe concerning unexcused school absences?——concerning 等于 about，是介词，引出讨论对象；与 Q47 唯一的差异在限定词 unexcused，读题时务必圈出。
questions.定位: P8 We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. 我们认为，无故缺勤是孩子和家庭所面临诸多挑战的强烈信号，包括经济与医疗方面的困难。

locate.en: We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships.
locate.zh: 我们认为，无故缺勤是孩子和家庭所面临诸多挑战的强烈信号，包括经济与医疗方面的困难。

option_analysis.note: They are likely to cause a decrease in students' academic achievements due to missed instruction 是作者明确反对的观点——It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction 中 "matters less as a cause" 直接否定了 "缺课通过 missed instruction 导致学业下降" 这一因果。A 项把作者反对的观点扣给作者本人。
B 项把 is a strong signal of 改写为 point directly to——"信号" 与 "指向" 是六级常见的隐喻互换，与预判 "无故缺勤指向校外挑战" 完全吻合。

pairs.orig: the many challenges children and families face
pairs.opt: many of the out-of-school challenges confronting children and their families

option_analysis.note: 原文未说政府 typically ignores unexcused absences——恰恰相反，P10 说政策 hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss，是 "管太严" 而非 "忽视"。C 项凭空捏造 "政府忽视" 这一事实。
原文 is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face 用一般现在时 face，指 "当下面对" 的挑战；D 项改成 the crises they are likely to face in the future 把时间挪到未来——把 "反映当下危机" 偷换成 "预测未来危机"。

questions.stem: What is the assumption underlying education policies in the U.S.?
questions.stem_zh: 美国教育政策所基于的假设是什么?

options.text: Children's academic performance depends on reducing the number of absences.
options.zh: 儿童的学业表现取决于减少缺勤次数。

options.text: Schools can boost children's academic performance by effective intervention.
options.zh: 学校可以通过有效干预提高儿童的学业表现。

options.text: Schools as well as families should be held responsible for out-of-school crises.
options.zh: 学校和家庭都应对校外危机负责。

options.text: Children's academic performance is closely related to the quality of instruction.
options.zh: 儿童的学业表现与教学质量密切相关。

questions.判型: What is the assumption underlying education policies in the U.S.? 问的是原文已经写明的预设，不是要读者推断政策背后的隐含逻辑。
questions.拆句: 结构是 What is the assumption underlying education policies in the U.S.?——主语是 the assumption，underlying 是现在分词作后置定语（= that underlies），限定 assumption 是 "作为政策基础的" 那种预设；不要把 underlying 误读为时间状语。
questions.定位: P11 They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. 这些政策还预设，学校能通过减少学生缺勤来有效进行干预。

locate.en: They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences.
locate.zh: 这些政策还预设，学校能通过减少学生缺勤来有效进行干预。

option_analysis.note: 原文 missing school for any reason harms children academically 是 "缺课损学业"——A 项 Children's academic performance depends on reducing the number of absences 把它倒过来说 "学业取决于减少缺勤"，表面相近但因果主语错位：原文主语是 "缺课"，A 项主语变成 "学业"，且 depends on 把单向因果偷换为 "取决于" 这一更强的依存关系。
B 项把第二个 assume（学校能有效干预）与前一句的因果（缺课损学业）合起来——干预 → 减少缺勤 → 提升学业，是政策预设的完整逻辑，与预判吻合。

pairs.orig: schools will be able to effectively intervene
pairs.opt: Schools can boost children's academic performance by effective intervention

pairs.orig: by reducing student absences + These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically

option_analysis.note: 原文 hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss 说政策让学校和家庭对 "缺课天数" 负责，而不是对 out-of-school crises 负责——"out-of-school crises" 是 out-of-school challenges 里的概念，C 项把它扣到了 "政策让学校家庭负责的对象" 头上，移花接木。
原文从头到尾在讨论 attendance / absences / missed instruction（错过的教学），从未讨论 the quality of instruction（教学质量）——D 项凭空引入 "教学质量" 概念，与原文核心论域无关。

questions.stem: What do the authors suggest doing regarding school absences?
questions.stem_zh: 作者建议如何处理学校缺勤问题?

options.text: Identifying their underlying causes.
options.zh: 找出其根本原因。

options.text: Reframing school attendance policies.
options.zh: 重新制定学校出勤政策。

options.text: Directing resources to helping needy children.
options.zh: 将资源用于帮助有需要的儿童。

options.text: Pressuring schools to reduce unexcused ones.
options.zh: 向学校施压以减少无故缺勤。

questions.判型: What do the authors suggest doing regarding school absences? 问的是作者明说的建议，原文有原句，不需推断。
questions.拆句: 结构是 What do the authors suggest doing regarding school absences?——suggest doing 是 suggest 接动名词的固定搭配，What 在动名词 doing 后充当宾语；regarding = about，限定话题。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P13 We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most. 我们反而建议：把无故缺勤作为信号，把资源调配给最需要这些资源的孩子和家庭。

locate.en: We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.
locate.zh: 我们反而建议：把无故缺勤作为信号，把资源调配给最需要这些资源的孩子和家庭。

option_analysis.note: 原文 P13 的建议是 "把 unexcused absence 当信号 → 把资源调配给需要者"，不是 Identifying their underlying causes（找缺勤的根本原因）——作者已经在前文给出原因（家庭/社区危机），末段不再建议 "找原因"，而是 "用信号导资源"。
原文 P10–P12 批评了现行政策，但 We instead suggest 的建议内容是 "用 unexcused absence 当信号导资源"，而不是 Reframing school attendance policies（重构考勤政策）——作者直接给出替代做法，没把 "重构政策" 作为建议本身提出。
C 项把 channel resources to 直接对应 Directing resources to，把 who need them most 压缩为 needy——两步同义改写都是六级高频考法，与预判完全吻合。

pairs.orig: the children and families who need them most

option_analysis.note: 原文 P12 明确指出现行政策 pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often 是负面后果，作者是 "批评施压"——D 项 Pressuring schools to reduce unexcused ones 反而把 "施压学校" 作为作者的建议，与原文立场完全相反。

reading2.title: 2025年6月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: After earning a bachelor's degree, I was determined to do what I love. I headed straight to graduate school to investigate the social problems that fascinated me.
passages.zh: 获得学士学位后，我下定决心去做自己热爱的事情。我径直进入研究生院，研究那些令我着迷的社会问题。

passages.en: For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. "Follow your passion," I counseled. "You can figure out the employment stuff later."
passages.zh: 将近十年的时间里，我告诉我遇到的每一个人，他们也应该这样做。“追随你的热情，”我劝告道。“就业方面的事情以后再想办法解决。”

passages.en: It wasn't until I began to research this widely accepted career advice that I understood how problematic it really was.
passages.zh: 直到我开始研究这一广为接受的职业建议，我才明白它实际上存在多么严重的问题。

passages.en: As a sociologist, I interviewed college students and professional workers to learn what it really meant to pursue their dreams, which I will refer to here as the passion principle. I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.
passages.zh: 作为一名社会学家，我采访了大学生和职场人士，以了解追逐梦想究竟意味着什么；在本文中，我将其称为“热情原则”。在为我的新书进行研究时，我对自己发现的有关这一原则的情况感到震惊。

passages.en: Surveys show the American public has long held the passion principle in high regard as a career decision-making priority. And its popularity is even stronger among those facing job instability.
passages.zh: 调查显示，美国公众长期以来一直高度重视“热情原则”，将其视为职业决策中的优先事项。而在那些面临就业不稳定的人群中，这一原则更受欢迎。

passages.en: Advocates of the passion principle found it compelling because they believed that following one's passion can provide workers with both the motivation necessary to work hard and a place to find fulfillment.
passages.zh: “热情原则”的倡导者认为它很有说服力，因为他们相信，追随自己的热情既能为劳动者提供努力工作的必要动力，也能为他们提供获得满足感的途径。

passages.en: Yet, what I found is that following one's passion does not necessarily lead to fulfillment, but is one of the most powerful cultural forces perpetuating overwork. I also found that promoting the pursuit of one's passion helps perpetuate social inequalities due to the fact that not everyone has the same economic resources to allow them to pursue their passion with ease.
passages.zh: 然而，我发现，追随自己的热情并不一定会带来满足感，反而是延续过度工作的最强大文化力量之一。我还发现，鼓励人们追随自己的热情，会助长社会不平等，因为并不是每个人都拥有同样的经济资源，能够轻松地追逐自己的热情。

passages.en: While the passion principle is broadly popular, not everyone has the necessary resources to turn their passion into a stable, good-paying job. Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs. Surveys revealed that working-class and first-generation college graduates, regardless of their career field, are more likely than their wealthier peers to end up in low-paying unskilled jobs when they pursue their passion.
passages.zh: 尽管“热情原则”广受欢迎，但并不是每个人都拥有将自己的热情转化为稳定且薪酬丰厚工作的必要资源。来自富裕家庭的热情追逐者更有能力等待自己热爱的工作出现，而不必担心这期间的学生贷款。他们也更有条件接受无薪实习，以便在父母为其支付房租的同时进入这个行业。此外，他们通常还能利用父母的社交网络来寻找工作。调查显示，无论所从事的职业领域如何，工薪阶层家庭出身的大学毕业生和第一代大学毕业生，在追随自己的热情时，比家庭更富裕的同龄人更有可能最终从事低薪的非技术性工作。

passages.en: Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the "follow your passion" path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.
passages.zh: 那些向所有人宣传“追随你的热情”这条道路，却不努力创造公平竞争环境的高校、工作场所和职业顾问，助长了职业追求者之间的社会经济不平等。

passages.en: It's not just well-off passion-seekers who benefit from the passion principle. Employers of passionate workers do, too. Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay. They even sacrifice a good salary, job stability and leisure time to work in a job they love.
passages.zh: 从“热情原则”中获益的不仅仅是经济条件优越的热情追逐者，热情洋溢的员工的雇主也同样受益。潜在雇主对充满热情的求职者表现出更大的兴趣，部分原因在于他们认为这些求职者会努力工作，却不会要求加薪。他们甚至会牺牲丰厚的薪水、工作的稳定性和闲暇时间，去从事一份自己热爱的工作。

questions.stem: What did the author advise people do for almost a decade?
questions.stem_zh: 作者在近十年里建议人们做什么?

options.text: Figure out what is the most fascinating job.
options.zh: 弄清楚什么是最令人着迷的工作。

options.text: Follow widely accepted career counsel.
options.zh: 遵循广泛接受的职业建议。

options.text: Pursue their careers with passion.
options.zh: 满怀热情地追求自己的职业。

options.text: Do whatever they are zealous for.
options.zh: 做任何他们热衷的事情。

questions.判型: What did the author advise people do for almost a decade 用 What did 直接问事实，没有 infer/suggest/imply/mainly about 等推断或主旨信号。
questions.拆句: What did the author advise people do for almost a decade 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 the author advise people do，advise sb. do 处省略 to（口语化结构），for almost a decade 是时间状语修饰整个动作，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. "Follow your passion," I counseled. "You can figure out the employment stuff later." 在将近十年的时间里，我告诉我遇到的每一个人：他们应该和我做一样的事。我劝告说：「追随你的激情」「就业那些事儿你以后再琢磨」。

locate.en: For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. "Follow your passion," I counseled. "You can figure out the employment stuff later."
locate.zh: 在将近十年的时间里，我告诉我遇到的每一个人：他们应该和我做一样的事。我劝告说：「追随你的激情」「就业那些事儿你以后再琢磨」。

option_analysis.note: Figure out what is the most fascinating job 把 fascinated 这个形容作者自己研究方向的词嫁接到 job 上，原文 P2 是作者劝别人 follow passion，不是劝别人去找最有趣的工作。
Follow widely accepted career counsel 把作者自己当年发出的建议描述为去跟随别人的建议，但原文 I counseled 表明作者本人就是 counsel 的发出者。
Pursue their careers with passion 是『用激情去追求事业』，原文是『追随你的激情』，二者并不等价：前者是把激情当工作态度，后者是把激情当工作方向。
预判答案是『追随激情/做自己热爱的事』，Do whatever they are zealous for 用 zealous for 同义替换 passion，正中预判。

pairs.opt: Do whatever they are zealous for

questions.stem: How did the author feel about the passion principle through his research?
questions.stem_zh: 作者通过研究对热情原则有何感受?

options.text: He was astonished by its consequences.
options.zh: 他对其后果感到震惊。

options.text: He was further convinced of its soundness.
options.zh: 他进一步确信了其合理性。

options.text: He was actually right to follow it through.
options.zh: 他贯彻执行它实际上是正确的。

options.text: He was struck by its broad popularity.
options.zh: 他对其广泛流行感到震撼。

questions.判型: How did the author feel about the passion principle through his research 直接问研究后的具体感受，是有明确指向的事实题。
questions.拆句: How did the author feel about the passion principle through his research 是 How 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 the author feel about the passion principle，through his research 作方式状语，限定感受产生的途径，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P4 I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book. 在为新书做的研究中，我被自己关于这一原则的发现震惊了。

locate.en: I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.
locate.zh: 在为新书做的研究中，我被自己关于这一原则的发现震惊了。

option_analysis.note: 预判是『被研究发现震惊』，astonished by its consequences 把震惊源具体落到 consequences 上，与原文 P7 起列举的负面后果一致。

pairs.orig: I was stunned by what I found out
pairs.opt: He was astonished by its consequences

option_analysis.note: He was further convinced of its soundness 说作者更加确信激情原则的正确性，但原文 how problematic it really was 与 stunned 均显示作者发现了它的问题，立场是反向的。
He was actually right to follow it through 说作者证实自己当初跟随激情是对的，但原文 does not necessarily lead to fulfillment 表明作者得出的是『追随激情未必带来满足』的反思结论，并非自我肯定。
He was struck by its broad popularity 把震惊对象错挂到『大众接受度』上，但题干问的是 through his research，原文 P5 谈大众接受度但用的是中性动词 hold ... in high regard，作者并未对此 struck。

questions.stem: What is important to turning one's passion into a stable, good-paying job?
questions.stem_zh: 将热情转化为稳定、高薪工作的关键是什么?

options.text: Willingness to take unpaid internships and low-paying jobs.
options.zh: 愿意接受无薪实习和低薪工作。

options.text: Full academic preparedness and sound career counseling.
options.zh: 充分的学业准备和合理的职业咨询。

options.text: Hard work and sacrifice of leisure time.
options.zh: 努力工作和牺牲休闲时间。

options.text: Financial backing and social connections.
options.zh: 经济支持和社会关系。

questions.判型: What is important to turning one's passion into a stable, good-paying job 问的是某事的关键条件，是事实层面的细节题。
questions.拆句: What is important to turning one's passion into a stable, good-paying job 中 turning ... job 是动名词短语作介词 to 的宾语，a stable, good-paying job 中两个形容词并列修饰 job，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P8 Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs. 出身富裕家庭的激情追随者更有能力等到自己真正热爱的工作出现，同时不必担心助学贷款；他们也更有条件接受无薪实习以打开职业大门，因为有父母替他们付房租；而且，他们往往可以借助父母的社会人脉帮自己找工作。

locate.en: Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs.
locate.zh: 出身富裕家庭的激情追随者更有能力等到自己真正热爱的工作出现，同时不必担心助学贷款；他们也更有条件接受无薪实习以打开职业大门，因为有父母替他们付房租；而且，他们往往可以借助父母的社会人脉帮自己找工作。

option_analysis.note: Willingness to take unpaid internships and low-paying jobs 把『愿意做无薪实习和低薪工作』当成转化成功的关键，但原文里无薪实习是富裕者的专利（while their parents pay their rent），而低薪非技能岗位则是工薪阶层 end up in low-paying unskilled jobs 的不利结局，二者都不是『成功条件』。
Full academic preparedness and sound career counseling 提到的『学业准备充分』在 P8 中根本没有任何线索；P9 虽出现 career counselors 但是被批评的对象、不是关键条件。
Hard work and sacrifice of leisure time 在原文中是 P10 雇主对激情员工的期待与员工实际付出的代价，与题 53 问的『把激情变成稳定高薪』的关键条件无关。
预判要点是经济和人脉两个维度，Financial backing and social connections 一项即覆盖两条，是与原文论据结构最完整匹配的概括。

pairs.orig: wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans
access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs

questions.stem: What happens when everyone is encouraged to follow their passion?
questions.stem_zh: 当每个人都被鼓励追随自己的热情时会发生什么?

options.text: Many more career aspirants end up unemployed.
options.zh: 更多的职业追求者最终失业。

options.text: People are less concerned with socioeconomic inequality.
options.zh: 人们不太关心社会经济不平等。

options.text: Socioeconomic inequality is likely to persist.
options.zh: 社会经济不平等可能持续存在。

options.text: Career counselors are going to lose credibility.
options.zh: 职业顾问将失去公信力。

questions.判型: What happens when everyone is encouraged to follow their passion 问的是一个已发生在原文里的具体结果，不需推断。
questions.拆句: What happens when everyone is encouraged to follow their passion 是 What 引导的疑问句加 when 时间从句，主干 What happens，everyone is encouraged to follow their passion 是被动语态从句，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P9 Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the "follow your passion" path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants. 那些向所有人推行『跟随激情』路径却不去拉平起跑线的高校、用人单位与职业顾问，正在加剧职业追求者之间的社会经济不平等。

locate.en: Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the "follow your passion" path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.
locate.zh: 那些向所有人推行『跟随激情』路径却不去拉平起跑线的高校、用人单位与职业顾问，正在加剧职业追求者之间的社会经济不平等。

option_analysis.note: Many more career aspirants end up unemployed 中的『失业』在原文中没有出现，P8 只说工薪阶层会落入 low-paying unskilled jobs（低薪非技能岗），那是有工作而非失业。
People are less concerned with socioeconomic inequality 说人们对不平等的关注度下降，原文 P9 说的是不平等本身被延续，并不涉及关注度的变化，且 less 反向于作者的批评立场。
预判结果是『不平等被延续』，C 用 persist 同义、用 is likely to 对应 help 的中等程度，结构性等值，是 54 的最佳概括。

pairs.opt: Socioeconomic inequality is likely to persist

option_analysis.note: Career counselors are going to lose credibility 推断职业顾问会失去公信力，原文 P9 只是批评他们推行『跟随激情』而不拉平起跑线，并未说他们会丧失公信力。

questions.stem: What does the author say about employers of passionate workers?
questions.stem_zh: 作者对雇用充满热情的员工的雇主有何看法?

options.text: They provide these workers with job stability and a good salary.
options.zh: 他们为这些员工提供工作稳定性和良好的薪水。

options.text: They exploit these workers' passion to benefit themselves.

options.text: They encourage these workers to realize their aspirations.
